gallery.title: File:"Old" Brooke Army Medical Center building.jpg
gallery.description: San Antonio Brooke Army Hospital/Medical Center, at right, was the center of medical research and training from 1948-1996. The red-roofed seventh-floor apartment (8 beds and a private sundeck) was used by Lyndon Johnson during his presidency and by seriously injured Army POWs returning from Vietnam. The world-class burn center cared for those injured during the ill-fated 1980 attempt to rescue U.S. hostages in Iran. Today the "old" BAMC is home to United States Army South and a number of smaller units.

gallery.title: File:100302-F-5640T-313 (4424701461).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: Saluting after laying a wreath to mark the 100th Anniversary of Miliitary Aviation are U.S. Air Force General  Stephen R. Lorenz, left, commander of AETC and Army Maj. Gen. Russell Czerw, commander of Fort Sam Houston. The anniversary celebration of military aviation featured a display of a reproduction Wright Flyer aircraft at Fort Sam Houston, Texas, and a flyover of another more air worthy model of the aircraft flown by the Wright Brothers at Kitty Hawk . On March 2, 1910 Army Lt. Benjamin Foulois made the first military flight at Fort Sam Houston in a Wright Flyer.

gallery.title: File:64 African American soldiers of the 24th Infantry Regiment (United States) on trial at Fort Sam Houston on 23 August 1917, from- Largest Murder Trial in the History of the United States - NARA - 533485 (cropped).tif
gallery.artist: Unknown authorUnknown author or not provided
gallery.description: Scope and content:  The full caption for this item is as follows: Largest Murder Trial in the History of the United States. Scene during Court Martial of 64 members of the 24th Infantry United States of America on trial for mutiny and murder of 17 people at Houston, Texas August 23, 1917. Trial held in Gift Chapel Fort Sam Houston. Trial started November 1, 1917, Brigadier General George K. Hunter presiding. Colonel J.A. Hull, Judge Advocate, Council for Defense, Major Harvy S. Grier. Major D.V. Sutphin, Assistant Advocate. Prisoners guarded by 19th Infantry Company C, Captain Carl J. Adler.
